analysis.title: GS Basics Brazil. What Will Break. Extreme Breadth
key_insights: NFP on Friday was soft: payrolls below consensus, unemployment ticked up and participation improved. That reduced pressure on the near-term Fed path and steepened the curve further.

Energy is still the key tail risk. Tankers were hit and escalation was threatened, but diplomatic channels remain open and oil is leaving the Gulf. That keeps the extreme energy tail from worsening for now, and oil is slightly lower.
TSMC rose 3% in Taiwan to a new all-time high. Privorotsky reads a breakout ahead of September sales as a sign the AI complex is not a fade.

The euro is falling on a possible Spanish snap election and French fiscal worries. France is the bigger issue, with the OAT/Bund spread widening. This week depends on whether any alternative French candidate offers a credible fiscal path. Lane speaks this morning.
Sentiment is negative: CNN Fear/Greed in the 30s, AAII Bull/Bear at -11.5, GS sentiment at -0.7 standard deviations.
Fundamental long/short funds cut almost 2 points of gross exposure last week. US fundamental net exposure is near the 2nd percentile of the last 5 years, and funds sold tech to cover macro shorts.

Breadth is split. More than half the Russell is 20% below its highs while the Nasdaq is breaking out. Breadth gives little reliable forward signal, but three months later markets have historically been higher and midterm seasonals from here are supportive.

Brazil first-round poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro at 47.0% and Lula at 45.2%, better for markets than expected. Brazil should be up sharply and the market will front-load the second round. This should support BRL, domestic equities and regional risk assets, and he suggests looking at second-order Brazil plays across Europe.

Rates: last week's steepener followed softer core PCE, supportive Williams and Jefferson comments and NFP below consensus. It was not the bull steepener one would hope for given the back-end selloff. A steeper curve can coexist with a more supportive Fed path if markets still expect strong nominal growth and earnings.
Credit calmed at the end of last week, but HY and CCC need close monitoring.

AI: TSMC/Terafab chatter supports semis. Nvidia-backed Reflection AI is reportedly preparing its first open-weight frontier model, which could compete with the strongest Chinese open-weight models. Samsung preliminary numbers and TSMC September sales arrive Thursday.

Treasury supply this week: $58bn 3-year Tuesday, $39bn 10-year Wednesday and $22bn 30-year Thursday, after some mediocre recent auctions. ISM Services today will show whether it confirms the price acceleration seen in manufacturing.

Risk view: selling a little into the Nasdaq rally is sensible, but positioning is still extremely light, macro shorts are large and Russell positioning is near the bottom of its recent range. He expects a market that grinds higher. He expects very good Q3 earnings. His view changes if sentiment turns euphoric or positioning gets stretched.
Other risks: France and European sovereign risk are harder to dismiss, and Eastern Europe remains a concern.

market_movers.rationale: TSMC broke out to a new all-time high, up 3% in Taiwan, ahead of September sales on Thursday. Privorotsky reads this as a clean signal from the AI complex.
Nvidia-backed Reflection AI is reportedly preparing its first open-weight frontier model, which could compete with the strongest Chinese open-weight models.

earnings_insights: Privorotsky expects Q3 2026 earnings season, which is around the corner, to produce very good numbers. No specific EPS or revenue figures are given.
Samsung preliminary numbers and TSMC September sales are due Thursday as hard data for the AI complex.
